hypothesis.title: frontend 2.0.4 rollout throws TypeError on null currencyCode in ProductPrice.tsx
hypothesis.summary: Frontend deployment 2.0.4 rolled out 9 minutes before the alert and introduced a TypeError in ProductPrice.tsx:22 when attempting to read 'currencyCode' from a null object. This error occurs on product pages and propagates as 5xx responses upstream to frontend-proxy, causing the alert to fire. The error rate jumped from 0.4% to ~7% in both frontend and frontend-proxy. Traces confirm frontend is the origin of 92-93% of failures.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend-proxy with a 5xx spike from 0.4% to 6.1%. Traces show that 92% of failing frontend-proxy traces end in the frontend service, and 93% of failing frontend traces also end in frontend itself. The deepest error in multiple traces is "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'currencyCode') at ProductPrice.tsx:22". This error appears 1,701 times in frontend logs starting 9 minutes before the alert, which coincides exactly with the frontend deployment rollout from 2.0.3 to 2.0.4 (also 9 minutes before the alert). The error is a JavaScript null-pointer dereference in a React component that renders product prices, indicating the frontend code is trying to access a currencyCode property on a null object. The ad service also deployed 2.0.2 → 2.0.3 at the same time, but ad's own error rate remains stable at 0.4% and its metrics are healthy, so that deployment is a red herring. The currency config change (DEFAULT_CURRENCY 'USD' → 'USD') is a no-op. The cart gRPC message-size errors started 44 minutes before the alert and predate the incident. The recommendation pod restart (exit 137, OOMKilled) is unrelated since recommendation is not on the failing trace paths. This matches the pattern of PM-2026-01-20 (bad deploy causing TypeError) and PM-2026-08-02 (bad release breaking currency integration). The root cause is the frontend 2.0.4 deployment introducing a bug in ProductPrice.tsx.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Frontend rolled out version 2.0.4 exactly 9 minutes before the alert, matching the timing of the first error logs and the error-rate spike.

1,701 occurrences of 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading currencyCode) at ProductPrice.tsx:22' starting 9 minutes before the alert, pinpointing the code defect introduced in the new release.
Failing trace shows the error originates in the frontend service span with the same TypeError, confirming frontend is the source, not just a symptom.
93% of failing frontend traces end in frontend itself, proving the fault is internal to frontend rather than a downstream dependency.
Frontend error rate jumped from 0.4% to 6.9% at -5m, correlating with the deployment and the error logs, demonstrating the impact of the bad release.

suggested_actions.title: Rollback frontend deployment to version 2.0.3
suggested_actions.rationale: The TypeError was introduced in 2.0.4 and did not exist in 2.0.3. Rolling back will immediately stop the errors.

suggested_actions.title: Verify frontend pods are healthy after rollback
suggested_actions.rationale: Confirm that the rollback completes successfully and pods reach Ready state.

suggested_actions.title: Check frontend error rate returns to baseline
suggested_actions.rationale: Monitor logs to confirm the TypeError stops appearing after rollback, validating the fix.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Currency service is not shown in the failing trace paths and has no error logs or metrics indicating it is down or degraded. The config change was a no-op (USD → USD). The TypeError is in frontend's own ProductPrice.tsx code, not a currency service failure.
